chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'And We took from you a solemn covenant.'
He said: The covenant is the word with which the marriage tie is bound, and as for His Word 'solemn', it is the water of the man which he empties into his wife.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'solemn covenant' (mithaq ghaliz) in Surah An-Nisa verse 21 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the Quranic term 'mithaq ghaliz' (solemn covenant) in Surah An-Nisa, identifying the covenant as the marriage contract and 'ghaliz' (thick/strong) as the husband's semen. This interpretation underscores the physical and spiritual potency of the marital bond, linking the biological act to the sanctity of the legal agreement. It reflects the Shia tradition of connecting linguistic nuances in the Quran to practical aspects of family law and physiology.
